best_for: PC players who own EA games, including copies bought on Steam or Epic, and need EA's launcher installed to start them.
description:
The EA app is Electronic Arts' desktop platform for downloading and playing its games. EA says it is built for speed, with less time and fewer clicks between opening the app and jumping into a game.

Once you are signed in, you can see what your friends are playing, find EA's newest releases, and add them to your collection in a few clicks. Games can download automatically and update in the background, so they are ready when you sit down to play. The catalog includes titles such as EA SPORTS FC 27, Madden NFL 27, Battlefield 6, Apex Legends, Split Fiction and STAR WARS Jedi: Survivor.

points.title: Required for EA games on PC
points.text: EA games on PC run through the EA app, even when you bought them on Steam or the Epic Games Store. Launching one of those titles walks you through installing it. It took over from Origin, and games you bought on Origin carry over to your library.

points.title: An EA Account is the entry fee
points.text: The app is free, but you sign in with an EA Account before you can download or play anything. You can link that account to other gaming platforms to bring friends lists across.

points.title: EA Play is the paid add-on
points.text: EA Play is listed at USD 5.99 per month or USD 39.99 per year, with a game library, 10-hour trials of some new releases and 10% off EA digital purchases. EA Play Pro is USD 16.99 per month or USD 119.99 per year and adds select new games on day one. A membership covers one platform. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: Windows needs 64-bit 10 or 11
points.text: EA lists a 64-bit PC with Windows 10 or Windows 11 as the minimum. The Windows installer sets the app up for all users, x64 only. The Windows listing keeps 137 versions.

points.title: The Mac app is thinner
points.text: There is a Mac version for macOS Catalina or newer, packaged as one universal installer for Intel and Apple silicon. Few EA games have Mac versions, so check a game's store page before you count on it. Only the current Mac release is listed here.
